addedLines: - chiron: Chiron (hera-triage) — post-session self-improvement agent for the HERA stack. Archives the session, builds the triage queue from all note streams, drafts dispositions and diffs, walks the human through rulings, lands the amendments, and keeps the corpus from growing monotonically. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- hera-session: HERA session-init — the front door for a measurement session. Interviews rig / device / brief / autonomy, builds the session dir with hera-mksession, fills the notebook's device slots from the device card, preflights JupyterLab, and hands off to hera-tactical. (Tools: All tools)

- hera-tactical: HERA tactical — drives measurement sessions with a human operator at the controls. Protocol only; machine facts come from the deployed rig card. Campaign scope set by the session brief. Reads rig card, device card, and live notebook; lands runnable cells via nb-collab. (Tools: All tools)

- iris: IRIS — chat-first collaborator for live toploader measurement sessions. Boots from prior state, follows the operator's lead, types cells when asked. Same tool surface as HERA tactical but inverted social contract — the human drives, IRIS supports. (Tools: All tools)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

content.content:
# Rig card — VTI

*Rig-level machine facts for the Sharpe Lab VTI (variable-temperature
insert) cryostat. Canonical copy: `hera/rig-cards/VTI.md` in the
`measurement-env` repo; deployed as `rig_card.md` next to
`device_card.md` in the measurement directory. Errors or gaps found
in-session go to `session_notes.md`, not this file — agents are
read-only on the repo.*

## Identity
- **Rig**: VTI — wet variable-temperature insert, out-of-plane magnet
- **Rig owner**: Bingcheng (VTI czar) — adjudicates envelope and
  operating-edge questions
- **Control PC**: `dgg-vti` (Windows 11); measurement dirs under
  `~/VTI_local_data/<user>/<session>/`
- **Base temperature**: ≈ 1.2–1.3 K; electron temperature ≈ 8 K
- **Status**: in service

## Magnet

- **Supply / driver**: CAEN ELS FAST-PS 1K5, `drivers.FastBi1K5`
  (raw TCP `192.168.0.10:10001`). Out-of-plane field, Tesla, via the
  `mag` qcodes Parameter.
- **Coil constant**: `T_per_A = 1/7.3` ≈ 0.137 T/A.
- **Ramp rate**: fixed 1 A/min ≈ **0.137 T/min**, hard-coded in the
  driver and sent with every setpoint. An 8 T traverse is a ~58 min
  floor.
- **Set semantics**: `magnet.mag(target)` **blocks** until the field
  is reached (busy-polls the ramping flag, then 3 s dwell). A cell
  that ramps is busy the whole ramp.
- **Interrupt ≠ stop**: interrupting the notebook cell does **not**
  stop the supply — it keeps ramping to the last setpoint. There is no
  abort/pause/ramp-to-zero method; recovery is calling `mag()` again
  with a new target. Aborting a ramp is the operator acting on the
  instrument, never a kernel interrupt.
- **Magnet limit**: **14.0 T** (Zack ruling 2026-06-12), enforced by
  the driver (`max_field_T = 14.0`; `mag()` raises above it). The
  session cap (device card / SAFETIES, machine-enforced via
  `magnet.mag.vals`) is what measurements obey.
- **Read-truth**: `mag()`'s get returns the **measured** output

# slot: gate-bindings — role aliases (k_tg/k_bg/k_si) from the device card's
# Gate stack section (which instrument drives which gate). The dc205_volt
# wrapper is generic; the k_* role map is device-specific. Each value

# Sweepable top-gate parameter — appears in the data as column 'DC_bias'.
def dcbias(vg):
    dc205.ramp_voltage(vg)

dc205_volt = qcodes.Parameter('DC_bias', unit='V', set_cmd=dcbias)

# Gate role aliases (recipes use k_tg / k_bg / k_si):
k_tg = dc205_volt   # top gate <- DC205 (fast axis is dc205_volt, NOT k_tg.volt)   # <-- validate
k_bg = k_2400       # back gate <- Keithley 2400                                     # <-- validate
k_si = k_2410       # Si gate   <- Keithley 2410                                     # <-- validate

=== cell#18 slot=gate-validators id=ad4a04d542e04c7884da8c8928433b1a ===
# slot: gate-validators — operating limits from the device card's gate-
# operating-limits table; commit EXACTLY the card numbers. Each value
# `# <-- validate`. Instrument-level fences go on the RAW instruments
# (dc205 / k_2400 / k_2410); direct calls bypass the role-alias wrapper.
TG_MIN, TG_MAX = -6.0, +7.0    # top gate (dc205_volt), V    # <-- validate
BG_MIN, BG_MAX = -4.5, +4.5    # back gate (k_2400), V        # <-- validate
SI_MIN, SI_MAX = -50.0, +50.0  # Si gate (k_2410), V          # <-- validate
dc205_volt.vals = validators.Numbers(TG_MIN, TG_MAX)
dc205.voltage.vals = validators.Numbers(TG_MIN, TG_MAX)  # instrument-level: direct dc205 calls bypass dc205_volt
k_2400.volt.vals = validators.Numbers(BG_MIN, BG_MAX)
k_2410.volt.vals = validators.Numbers(SI_MIN, SI_MAX)

# Limit lists for sanitize_tg_bg()
tg_lims, bg_lims = [TG_MIN, TG_MAX], [BG_MIN, BG_MAX]

# Session field cap — machine-enforced: magnet.mag is a qcodes Parameter,
# so this validator rejects any magnet.mag(target) with |B| > B_SESSION_CAP
# before any hardware traffic. (Driver max_field_T = 14.0 remains as backstop.)
B_SESSION_CAP = 8.0  # Tesla    # <-- validate (session cap from card/brief)
magnet.mag.vals = validators.Numbers(-B_SESSION_CAP, B_SESSION_CAP)

# Temperature setpoint cap — TYPO GUARD ONLY (sample_setpoint(3000) vs 300).
# The real safe T/B envelope is a rig-card item.
T_SESSION_CAP = 310.0  # K    # <-- verify

# Device card — QC0426 (trilayer graphene)

*Session device card for QC0426 on the **VTI** cryostat. Deployed into the
measurement directory alongside the working notebooks. This card carries
**physical truth**: what is wired, the hardware, the outer safety box,
the provided gate operating limits, and the provided contact
configuration. The CNP location and (n, D) calibration are established
in-session (see the session brief).*

## Identity
- **Device id**: `QC0426`
- **Material**: trilayer graphene (`3LGr`).
- **Owner**: qingrui
- **Fridge**: VTI (variable-temperature insert). Base (sample)
  temperature ≈ 1.2–1.3 K.
- **Status**: cold, wired; no CNP location on record.

## Gate stack (three gates)
- **Top gate** (`k_tg`): hBN dielectric. **Driven by the SRS DC205** —
  in the data it appears as the column **`DC_bias`** (the
  DC205 voltage), and in sweep calls as `dc205_volt` (a
  `qcodes.Parameter` wrapping `k_tg.ramp_voltage`, `ramp_rate = 2`; the
  measure notebook's setup cells define it).
- **Back gate** (`k_bg`): thick graphite on hBN, driven by a **Keithley
  2400**.
- **Si global back gate** (`k_si` / `k_2410`): doped-Si gate through
  **SiO₂**, driven by a second Keithley (`k_2410`). The graphite back gate
  screens Si from the channel — Si couples only to the contacts
  (contact-doping gate). Operating limit provided (below).
- **Gate-stack geometry** (fabrication facts; **geometry prior only** —
  the capacitance *calibration* is the session's to establish via
  `cnp-and-dline-calibration`):
  ```python
  from sharpelab_nb.gates import stack_capacitance, calc_nD, calc_gate_voltages
  c_tg = stack_capacitance([(15.6, 3)])           # 15.6 nm hBN
  c_bg = stack_capacitance([(12, 3), (0, 3.9)])   # 12 nm hBN, no SiO2 term
  ```
  Treat anything derived from these (lever arms, n/D scales, CNP-line
  slope) as uncalibrated until the session's own gate map confirms it.

## Gate operating limits — gate B contract

Gate operating limits for the session:

| Parameter | Operating limit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `dc205_volt` / `k_tg` | **[−6.0, +7.0] V** | provided; geometry ceiling is the hard fence behind it |
| `k_bg.volt` | **[−4.5, +4.5] V** | provided |
| `k_2410.volt` (Si) | **[−50, +50] V** | provided |
| **B field (session cap)** | **\|B\| ≤ 8.0 T** | committed on the `magnet.mag` validator (SAFETIES); driver `max_field_T = 14.0` T is the hard backstop |

## Measurement setup (rig instruments wired this cooldown)
- **Gates**: top via **DC205** (`DC_bias`), back via **k_bg** Keithley,
  Si via **k_2410** Keithley.
- **AC excitation / lock-ins**: SR830 family (`sr0…sr3` live).
  Current-bias drive: **0.5 V through a 100 MΩ bias resistor**, lock-in
  frequency **≈ 13 Hz**.
- **Current channel**: **`sr0`** = drain current, **`sr0_gain = −1E6`**
  (Ithaco preamp gain). Per-channel sensitivities are recorded per run in
  `measurement_config`.
- **Lock-in time constant**: 0.3 s, 24 dB/oct, all channels (`sr0`–`sr3`).
  Minimum dwell 4·τ = 1.2 s/pt.
- **Sensitivity by signal scale**: CNP / gate-map (kΩ) ~2e-5 on the voltage
  channels; high-|n| metallic (tens of Ω) `sr1` 2e-6, `sr2` 5e-7, `sr3` 5e-6,
  `sr0` 1e-2.
- **Bias current**: 0.5 V / 5 nA through the 100 MΩ default; high-|n| metallic
  regime ~2 V / 20 nA.
- **Voltage channels**: `sr1, sr2, sr3` carry four-terminal voltages.
  `sr3` is the Hall channel (`r_xy`).
- **Contact switching — QSwitch (QDevil) mux** — ContactMux live:
  - Wiring topology (final per the operator's
    routing slide): device pads bond to two Fischer cables; the
    QSwitch takes **F1 only**, and F2-riding contact pads are shorted
    onto spare F1 conductors at the breakout. **F1 fischer index =
    QSwitch line number.** TG and BG do **not** pass through the
    QSwitch (hardwired to their sources — fixed, unswitchable). Si
    passes through the QSwitch and back to the breakout box.
  - **Contact map** (label = position, T = top arc L→R, B = left side
    then bottom L→R; all switchable):

    | Label | Pad | Line | | Label | Pad | Line |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | T1 | F2-05 | 1 | | B1 | F2-37 | 8 |
    | T2 | F1-33 | 3 | | B2 | F2-21 | 17 |
    | T3 | F1-09 | 4 | | B3 | F1-28 | 23 |
    | T4 | F1-01 | 6 | | B4 | F1-12 | 22 |
    | T5 | F1-42 | 7 | | B5 | F1-20 | 20 |
    | T6 | F1-02 | 12 | | B6 | F1-44 | 19 |
    | T7 | F1-43 | 13 | | B7 | F1-03 | 18 |
    | | | | | B8 | F1-35 | 15 |

    Alive: T2, T3, T4, T5, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7. Dead: T1, T6, T7, B1, B8
    (B2 high-R).

  - **Gates**: TG (DC205) and BG (K2400) **hardwired — no relay can
    touch them**. **Si (K2410) rides QSwitch lines 16 and 11** with
    standing closed relays ("keep 16/11 closed inside the QSwitch" —
    routed through the switch and back to the breakout box). Lines
    16/11 are **excluded from ContactMux's managed set** (never in the
    `lines` map), and **`qsw.reset()` is always forbidden** — it opens
    the standing closures and drops the Si gate.
  - **Instrument taps (BNC 1–8)**: 1 = sr1.V1, 2 = sr1.V2, 3 = sr2.V1,
    4 = sr2.V2, 5 = sr3.V1, 6 = sr3.V2, **7 = sr1.amplitude (AC
    source)**, **8 = sr0.V1 × −1e6 (measured AC current)**. ContactMux
    form: `breakouts = {"source": 7, "drain": 8, "sr1+": 1, "sr1-": 2,
    "sr2+": 3, "sr2-": 4, "sr3+": 5, "sr3-": 6}`.
  - `settle_s` **4 s**.
- **Provided contact configuration**:

  | role | label | QSwitch line |
  |---|---|---|
  | source | T2 | 3 |
  | drain (`sr0`) | B7 | 18 |
  | `sr1` (Rxx) | T3–T4 | 4, 6 |
  | `sr2` (Rxx) | B4–B5 | 22, 20 |
  | `sr3` (Rxy, Hall) | T5–B6 | 7, 19 |

  ContactMux form: `mux.select({"source": "T2", "drain": "B7", "sr1+":
  "T3", "sr1-": "T4", "sr2+": "B4", "sr2-": "B5", "sr3+": "T5", "sr3-":
  "B6"})`.
